Irelarui: Critical arui Philosophical (1881), Standish James O'Grady explains
that "Coelte, after the destruction of the Fians, entered the host of the
Tuatha De Danan, and lived immortal and invisible in the island. He stormed
the enchanted fortress of the gods of the Erne at Assaroe, and entered
himself into its possession, where he dwelt for many centuries." In On the
Manners arui Customs of the Ancient Irish (1873), Eugene O'Curry refers to
"Ilbhreac, a Tuath De Danann at Eas Ruaidh (now the Falls of Ballyshannon,
in the county Donegal)," which may explain Yeats's description of llbhreac
as "one of the children of the goddess Danu," Danu being the mother or
maternal ancestor of all the gods.
 Fergus mac Raoich is an important character in the Ulster Cycle of stories;
